description_good_justification: The README opens with what the library is: a Go implementation of EDHOC, the key exchange defined in RFC 9528.
interact_justification: The README explains how to get the library (go get), and https://github.com/aquilliam/edhoc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to report issues and send pull requests.
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/aquilliam/edhoc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md lists the checks to run, the testing requirement and the DCO sign-off.
documentation_interface_justification: Every exported identifier has a doc comment, published at https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/aquilliam/edhoc, with a runnable example in example_test.go.
sites_https_justification: The project is hosted on GitHub and pkg.go.dev, both HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests: https://github.com/aquilliam/edhoc/issues
english_justification: Documentation is in English, and bug reports and comments in English are accepted.
repo_track_justification: Git records who made each change and when.
repo_interim_justification: Work is committed to the public repository as it is done, not only at releases.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No vulnerabilities have been reported or fixed.
report_responses_justification: No bug reports have been filed yet. Reports are answered through GitHub issues.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests have been filed yet. Requests are answered through GitHub issues.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports go through GitHub private vulnerability reporting: https://github.com/aquilliam/edhoc/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received. SECURITY.md commits to a reply within five working days.
build_justification: The standard Go toolchain builds it: go build ./...
build_floss_tools_justification: The Go toolchain is free software.
test_justification: Unit tests, fuzz tests and the RFC 9529 test vectors run with go test ./... and are published in the repository.
test_most_justification: Statement coverage is about 88% for the main package and 84-95% for the internal packages. Tests include both RFC 9529 traces byte for byte, Wycheproof vectors, and tamper tests on every message.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs vet, the tests with the race detector, staticcheck and govulncheck on every push and pull request, on Linux, macOS and Windows: https://github.com/aquilliam/edhoc/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: https://github.com/aquilliam/edhoc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md requires a test for changes to message processing.
tests_are_added_justification: Each feature was added together with its tests, as the commit history shows.
warnings_justification: go vet and staticcheck run in CI.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any go vet or staticcheck finding, and the code is clean.
warnings_strict_justification: staticcheck runs with its default checks, and any finding fails CI.
crypto_published_justification: Only the algorithms of the RFC 9528 cipher suites are used: AES-CCM, AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, SHA-2, HKDF, X25519, P-256, P-384, EdDSA and ECDSA.
crypto_call_justification: Primitives come from the Go standard library and golang.org/x/crypto. The one exception is AES-CCM, which Go does not provide; it is built on crypto/aes and tested against RFC 3610 and Wycheproof.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography uses the Go standard library and golang.org/x/crypto, both free software.
crypto_keylength_justification: The minimum is 128-bit security: AES-128, P-256 and X25519, as RFC 9528 specifies.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithms such as MD5, SHA-1, DES or RC4 are used.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Only the current algorithms from RFC 9528 are used.
crypto_pfs_justification: Every EDHOC session uses fresh ephemeral Diffie-Hellman keys, which gives perfect forward secrecy.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The library does not store passwords.
crypto_random_justification: Ephemeral keys and signatures use crypto/rand.
delivery_mitm_justification: It is distributed as a Go module over HTTPS. The go command verifies downloads against the Go checksum database.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Downloads are over HTTPS and checked against the Go checksum database.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository holds no private credentials. Test keys come from the RFC 9529 public test vectors. GitHub secret scanning and push protection are enabled.
static_analysis_justification: go vet, staticcheck and govulncheck run on every push and pull request.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: govulncheck checks for known vulnerabilities in the code and its dependencies, and staticcheck catches common bug patterns.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No findings are open, and CI fails on any new finding.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every push and pull request.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Go fuzz targets cover the CBOR decoder, ID_CRED and CWT Claims Set parsing, CoAP payloads, AES-CCM and every EDHOC message, and tests run with the race detector. An interop test against lakers covers both roles.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The code is pure Go: no unsafe, no cgo and no assembly.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Fuzz targets check invariants such as encode and decode round trips and that an accepted message lets the session continue, and CI runs the tests with the race detector.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No vulnerabilities have been found by dynamic analysis.
version_unique_justification: Each release is a git tag (for example v0.1.0) that the Go module system uses as the version.
version_semver_justification: Releases follow semantic versioning, as Go modules require.
version_tags_justification: Releases are signed git tags: https://github.com/aquilliam/edhoc/tags
